title: The Environments screen shows what is set without ever showing a value
description:
SPIDR child 3 of task-9ae492b373fa4e7aa6b1e91585f6e612 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 (task-d0c63cd8848a4da18ad3fbb8eb1d95c3, the store and reads) and child 2 (task-72b22fcf9da54b3b91dabf5b7392aff1, required names and delivery). PROOF ROW: it owns the UI, the Playwright journey and the docs (global rail 21).

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: an Environments screen (per environment: required vs set, set/unset dialogs, fingerprint, last update) and the goal's 'N required variables unset for preview' with a link to it.

THE SCREEN NEVER SHOWS A VALUE, and it is the surface most likely to leak one: it is the only place an operator TYPES a value, so the input, its state, any error message and any browser devtools-visible prop must be considered. The reads child 1 built return {name, isSet, sha256 fingerprint, updatedAt} and no value - the screen must not add one back by echoing what was typed after a failed submit, which is the natural way to be helpful and the exact way this leaks into a screenshot.

THE FINGERPRINT IS THE OPERATOR'S ONLY FEEDBACK. Since they can never see the value back, the sha256 fingerprint changing after an update is how they know the update took. Render it, and make clear it is a fingerprint rather than a truncated value.

THE UNSET COUNT IS THE POINT OF THE GOAL CARD. 'N required variables unset for preview' is what stops a deploy failing for a reason nobody can see - the required names come from the approved contract via child 2.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04): the ops screens live at apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/ (ops-screens.tsx is 228 lines, close to the 250 ceiling - a new screen likely belongs in its own module rather than appended there), the live read clients in apps/control-room/src/live/ decode with EXACT-KEY checks, and every new route needs its pin in dev-proxy-paths.ts.
definitionOfDone: An Environments screen renders, per environment, the required-vs-set table with each variable's fingerprint and last update, plus set and unset dialogs, against a REAL daemon frame.

NO VALUE IS EVER RENDERED OR RETAINED: assert that after a FAILED submit the screen does not echo the typed value back, and that no value appears in the rendered output for any state. This is the leak this screen invites - echoing input after an error is the helpful-looking behaviour that puts a secret in a screenshot.

The fingerprint CHANGES in the UI after an update and is labelled as a fingerprint, not as a truncated value - the operator can never see the value back, so this is their only confirmation the update took.

The goal card shows 'N required variables unset for <environment>' with a link to the screen, driven by the required names child 2 reads from the approved contract; assert the count for a goal with two required names and one set, and assert the card is absent when none are required.

All four refusals render VERBATIM with their codes (ENV_NAME_INVALID, ENV_VALUE_TOO_LARGE, ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN, ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE) - and the refusal text must not contain the submitted value.

A Playwright journey against a REAL daemon covers the required-vs-set table, a set/unset round trip and the fingerprint changing on update; `pnpm test:e2e:browser` count line quoted. The new read's decoder is EXACT-KEY and its proxy pin is added to dev-proxy-paths.ts.

The runbook documents the environments model (environments, required names from the contract, fingerprints, and that values are never readable back); gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`.
taskRails: NEVER ECHO A TYPED VALUE BACK - not after a failed submit, not in a refusal message, not in a retained form state. This screen is the only place a value is typed and therefore the likeliest leak.
THE FINGERPRINT IS NOT A TRUNCATED VALUE. Label it so; an operator who thinks they are seeing part of the secret will treat the screen as unsafe to share, or worse, will not.
THIS ROW PROVES, IT DOES NOT REBUILD: a store or read defect is child 1's, a required-names or delivery defect is child 2's. Comment there and report_blocked.
ops-screens.tsx is 228 lines against a 250 ceiling - put a new screen in its own module rather than appending, and measure with `wc -l` before writing.
ASCII-only sources and apostrophe-free JSX text (scheduler package-boundary scan); check any new testid namespace is free; EXACT-KEY decoder plus a dev-proxy-paths pin for any new read.

implementationPlan.description:
PREREQUISITE HARD STOP. This row PROVES; it does not rebuild. Verify each prerequisite on disk and STOP if any is missing.

- `ls apps/daemon/src/http/ | grep -i env` and `git grep -n "/environments/read" -- apps/daemon/src` — the HTTP read (task-ef76a7f4523d46f48a2f9eb19595e801). At plan time this returned NOTHING, which is why that row exists. Confirm it is reachable from the COMPOSED production listener, not only from a hand-built test server — that distinction is exactly what forced task-eb2bb09d to exist after task-7ca9dca3.
- `git grep -rn "required" -- apps/daemon/src/environment` and whatever symbol child 2 (task-72b22fcf9da54b3b91dabf5b7392aff1) shipped for REQUIRED NAMES from the approved contract. It was still PLANNING at plan time and DoD 4 depends on it.
- `git grep -rn "ENV_NAME_INVALID\|ENV_VALUE_TOO_LARGE\|ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN\|ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE" -- apps/daemon/src/environment` — child 1's four codes and their CLOSED code->layer map. Record the exact layer each code carries; step 5 asserts code AND layer and must reuse this map rather than minting a second one.

If any is absent, `moe.report_blocked` with `blockedOnTaskIds`. Do NOT mock the read, do NOT hand-write a daemon frame, and do NOT narrow DoD 1 or 4 — a mock-backed journey proves the shape and retires the question unanswered.

Also measure before writing (rail 4): `wc -l apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/ops-screens.tsx` (236 at plan time against a 250 ceiling — the description's 228 is stale) and confirm the testid namespace you intend to claim is free with `git grep -c "cr\.<namespace>" -- apps tests`.

THE READ CLIENT: exact-key decoder plus the proxy pin (DoD 6, second half). Create the live read module under apps/control-room/src/live/ following the neighbouring live read clients.

EXACT-KEY DECODING: an unknown key and a missing key each REFUSE with a specific code, asserted with the code AND the layer that refused — never merely that decoding failed. The decoded shape is {name, isSet, sha256 fingerprint, updatedAt} per variable, per environment. THERE IS NO VALUE FIELD, and the decoder must not tolerate one: if the daemon ever grows a value field, this decoder should REFUSE rather than pass it through to a screen that might render it. Assert that as its own arm — it is the client-side half of epic rail 3.

ADD THE PROXY PIN to `DEV_PROXY_PATHS` in apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts (55 lines, frozen list at :5), keeping the file's existing ordering. Note `/design/read` is NOT pinned there, so a pin is not automatic for every route — DoD 6 requires one here deliberately, and without it the dev lane cannot reach the read at all.

NO VALUE IS RETAINED CLIENT-SIDE: no localStorage, no sessionStorage, no module-level cache of a submitted value. Copy the source-text assertion pattern from apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-publish.test.tsx:204-215 — readFileSync of your own module, then `not.toContain("localStorage")` / `"sessionStorage"`. That arm is cheap and it is the one that catches a helpful cache added later.

THE ENVIRONMENTS SCREEN (DoD 1) — its OWN module under apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/, NOT appended to ops-screens.tsx (236 lines against a 250 ceiling).

Render, per environment, the required-vs-set table: each variable's name, whether it is set, its sha256 FINGERPRINT and last update, plus set and unset dialogs.

THE FINGERPRINT IS THE OPERATOR'S ONLY FEEDBACK and it must be LABELLED AS A FINGERPRINT, not shown as a bare truncated-looking string (DoD 3, rail 2). An operator who believes they are seeing part of the secret will either treat the screen as unsafe to share or, worse, will not. Put the word in the rendered output and assert it — not in a comment.

Mount it as a route and register it wherever ops screens are registered; a screen no route reaches is dead code that satisfies every existence grep while the feature does not exist.

CONSTRAINTS (rail 5): ASCII-only sources; apostrophe-free JSX text — the scheduler package-boundary scan reds on an apostrophe in JSX and the red looks unrelated to the diff that caused it; the new testid namespace confirmed free in step 1; and `wc -l` under 250, quoted.

THE FINGERPRINT CHANGES, AND THE FOUR REFUSALS (DoD 3 and 5) — same test file.

FINGERPRINT (DoD 3): after an update, the rendered fingerprint CHANGES. Assert the before and after values differ AND that the new one matches what the read returned — not merely that something changed, which a re-render alone would satisfy. Because the operator can never see the value back, this is their only confirmation the update took. Also assert the fingerprint is labelled as a fingerprint in the rendered output.

REFUSALS (DoD 5): ENV_NAME_INVALID, ENV_VALUE_TOO_LARGE, ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN and ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE each render VERBATIM with their code plus operator words. Reuse child 1's CLOSED code->layer map recorded in step 1 — do not mint a second map, and do not invent a fifth code.

AND THE REFUSAL TEXT MUST NOT CONTAIN THE SUBMITTED VALUE. ENV_VALUE_TOO_LARGE is the trap: the natural message names the size and often quotes the offending input. Assert the sentinel is absent from each refusal message, and assert ENV_VALUE_TOO_LARGE reports the LIMIT rather than the value.

ENV_STORE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE deserves operator words that say what to do — it means the store key is missing, which is an operator-fixable condition, not a bug report.

THE GOAL CARD: 'N required variables unset for <environment>' (DoD 4). This is what stops a deploy failing for a reason nobody can see.

The required names come from the approved contract via child 2 (task-72b22fcf9da54b3b91dabf5b7392aff1) — read them from its surface, do not re-derive them from the contract here.

Render the count with a LINK to the Environments screen, and assert exactly what DoD 4 names:
(a) a goal with TWO required names and ONE set shows a count of ONE;
(b) the card is ABSENT when none are required — absent, not a zero badge. Assert absence by querying for the testid and finding nothing.
Also assert the card names the ENVIRONMENT it is counting for: 'unset for preview' and 'unset for production' are different facts and a card that omits which one it means invites the wrong fix.

The card renders NAMES and COUNTS only — never a value, never a fingerprint that could be mistaken for one.

Mount it on the goal beside the existing cards; check whether it belongs in the status-strip map at apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-status-strip.tsx:33 the way `publish` does, and say either way in the note.

THE JOURNEY (DoD 6) — a new spec under tests/e2e/control-room/, against a REAL daemon.

HARNESS: `withDaemonBackedControlRoom` / `DaemonLane` from ./daemon-ports.js. Drive the bare `lane.baseUrl` — main.tsx:101 serves the legacy shell only for `?v1=1`, so a journey clicking `cr.liveboard.*` re-proves the old dev board and leaves the shipped surface untested. Seat any dispatch recorder BEFORE the first click: a card's dispatch report lives only until the next surface poll re-keys the card (board-chain.spec.ts:26-33).

COVER: the required-vs-set table rendering from a real frame; a set/unset ROUND TRIP; and the fingerprint CHANGING on update. The round trip is the part that proves the screen and the daemon agree — a set that renders but does not persist, or an unset that leaves the row 'set', both pass a component test.

THEN THE LEAK CHECK AT THE REAL BOUNDARY: after typing a sentinel value in the browser, assert it appears in NO response body the page received and in NO page content. A component test cannot see the wire; this can.

TEARDOWN in a `finally`: the lane, the daemon child, and any store or temp directory it created — released on the throwing path too. A test that leaks a port makes every later gate on this board inadmissible (epic rail 4).

Quote the `pnpm test:e2e:browser` count line.

THE RUNBOOK AND THE GATES (DoD 7).

DOCS: `docs/agent-stack-runbook.md` documents the environments model — what an environment is, that required names come from the APPROVED CONTRACT (not from a config file), what the fingerprint is and what it is for, and, stated plainly, THAT VALUES ARE NEVER READABLE BACK. That last sentence is the one an operator needs before they type a secret into a browser: they must know the only way to verify an update is the fingerprint. Say what shipped, not what the design intended.

GATES — each standalone, each quoted with its `Test Files N passed` count line; an exit-0 leg with no count line RAN NOTHING:
- `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` — this row's primary evidence.
- `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm test:e2e:browser`
State explicitly that root `pnpm test` covers NO apps/** file, so the control-room leg carries the apps/** claim.

SIZE AND STYLE: `wc -l` every production file you created and quote it (250 ceiling). Confirm ASCII-only sources and apostrophe-free JSX text.

PATH-ATTRIBUTED BASELINE: repo-wide failures at the merge-base, at HEAD, subtract, intersect with this row's owned paths. Complete only when that intersection is EMPTY; disclose any foreign red verbatim with its failing file paths.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW before `moe.complete_task`. This screen handles secrets, so review it as someone trying to get a value out of it.

THE LEAK SURFACE, each answered with a command or an arm:
- Does the sentinel appear in ANY response body, console line, or page content after a full round trip? The journey can see the wire; use it.
- Does a FAILED submit retain the value anywhere — React state, an uncontrolled input's DOM value, a form's autocomplete, a retry buffer? Check the DOM after the failure, not just the React tree.
- Would a browser autofill or password manager capture the input? Check the input's `type` and `autocomplete` attributes and say what they are.
- Does any refusal message quote the input? ENV_VALUE_TOO_LARGE is the likeliest offender.
- Does the fingerprint reveal anything about the value — is it the full sha256, and is it labelled so no one reads it as a prefix of the secret?
- Is there a realistic-looking secret in ANY committed fixture (epic rail 3)? Grep your own new files.
- Does an error boundary or a logging hook serialize props that carry the value?

CORRECTNESS:
- Two operators setting the same variable concurrently — does the fingerprint the second sees reflect the first's write, or a stale read?
- An unset of a variable that is not set — defined answer, or a crash?
- A variable required by the contract but for an environment that does not exist — which refusal wins, and is that the useful one?

MUTATION DRILL: `git status --porcelain` the exact paths FIRST. Every file this row creates is NEW (untracked), so `git diff -- <path>` certifies NOTHING for them — back each mutated path up out of tree under %TEMP% suffixed by your worker id and prove the restore by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore. dev-proxy-paths.ts and the runbook are TRACKED, so `git diff` is a valid restore proof there.

comments.author: worker-b1872f24
comments.content:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW (step 9), worker-b1872f24. Every question answered by a command or an arm, not by reading the design.

--- THE LEAK SURFACE ---

1. SENTINEL IN ANY RESPONSE BODY / REQUEST / PAGE CONTENT AFTER A FULL ROUND TRIP? NO.
   tests/e2e/control-room/environment-variables.spec.ts records `page.on("response")` and
   `page.on("request")` BEFORE the first navigation, runs a real set/update/unset round trip
   against a real daemon, then asserts absence across every response body, every request body and
   `page.content()`. Two controls: the recorder is asserted non-empty, and a positive control
   proves the search would find a planted sentinel. Spec EXIT 0 (`1 passed (11.4s)`), and it is
   among the 31 passed in the full `pnpm test:e2e:browser` run.

2. DOES A FAILED SUBMIT RETAIN THE VALUE? NO - and this is the arm the row turns on.
   The typed value lives in ONE useState inside SetDialog. `settle()` clears `editing` on EVERY
   settled submit, which UNMOUNTS the dialog that owns it. Checked in the DOM, not only the React
   tree: after a refusal the arm asserts the dialog is gone, reopens it, and asserts the field's
   `.value` is "". Also covered on the UNDELIVERED branch (a thrown dispatch takes the other
   branch of settle()).
   MUTATION-DRILLED (step 4): `if (next.ok) setEditing(null)` made the two value arms go RED at
   `expected '<div class="cr2-card"...' not to contain 'SENTINEL-...'` - the sentinel search
   itself, not a helper precondition. Restored, sha256 3587c047...8248.

3. AUTOFILL / PASSWORD MANAGER? Attributes ASSERTED, not assumed:
   `type="password"`, `autocomplete="off"`, `spellcheck="false"`. No `name` that a heuristic
   autofill matches on (`cr-env-vars-value`), and no `form` wrapping a username field.

4. DOES ANY REFUSAL QUOTE THE INPUT? NO. All four ENV_ codes swept, each asserting its code AND
   layer present and the sentinel absent. ENV_VALUE_TOO_LARGE - the likeliest offender - reports
   the LIMIT from a constant ("under 4096 bytes"), and the arm additionally asserts the SUBMITTED
   LENGTH is absent: reporting the size of what was typed is a weaker leak but still a fact about
   it. The daemon's own details are digit-free by upstream assertion, which is why the limit has
   to come from this side at all.

5. DOES THE FINGERPRINT REVEAL ANYTHING? It is the FULL sha256 of the value's bytes, computed
   daemon-side from plaintext that is then dropped. The screen shows the first 12 chars LABELLED
   `sha256 fingerprint`, with title "A sha256 fingerprint of the stored value. It is not part of
   the value." Both asserted. Unset renders "Not set", never an empty-looking string. The goal
   CARD carries no fingerprint at all, with a control proving one IS present lower down - a
   fingerprint on a summary card is the thing most plausibly misread as a truncated secret.

6. REALISTIC-LOOKING SECRET IN A COMMITTED FIXTURE? NO. Grepped my own new files for
   `sk-|ghp_|AKIA|-----BEGIN|password=|api_key=`: zero hits. Sentinels are
   "SENTINEL-not-a-secret-..." shaped - unmistakably not a credential, so no scanner alert and no
   rail-3 breach.

7. ERROR BOUNDARY / LOGGING HOOK SERIALIZING PROPS? NONE EXISTS.
   `grep -rn "componentDidCatch|ErrorBoundary|getDerivedStateFromError|window.onerror"` over
   apps/control-room/src returns NOTHING. Separately, the value is never a prop at all: the
   fiber-walk arm asserts it IS findable while the dialog is open (proving the walker reaches
   props) and NOT findable after submit.

8. CLIENT-SIDE RETENTION? `grep localStorage|sessionStorage|indexedDB|console.|document.cookie`
   across all seven production files: zero hits. Plus a source-text arm on the read client.

--- CORRECTNESS ---

9. TWO OPERATORS SETTING THE SAME VARIABLE CONCURRENTLY. DISCLOSED, NOT FIXED, and not fixable
   here. The screen re-reads on every settled write (`onSettled`), so the fingerprint an operator
   sees after their OWN write is the daemon's post-write state, not a stale one. But there is NO
   lost-update detection: `runEnvironmentEdge` deliberately ignores `expectedVersion` and derives
   the aggregate from the principal, so B's write silently overwrites A's and B sees B's
   fingerprint. That is a daemon-seam property (child 1's), not this row's - a CAS would have to
   exist at the edge first. Flagging for the epic-final hardening row rather than filing a row.

10. UNSET OF A VARIABLE THAT IS NOT SET. DEFINED, no crash: `unsetEnvironmentVariable` validates
    scope then name, then appends an UNSET event and answers the read - idempotent. The screen
    only offers Unset on a row that reads set, so this needs a concurrent unset to reach.

11. REQUIRED BY THE CONTRACT BUT FOR AN ENVIRONMENT THAT DOES NOT EXIST. SCOPE WINS and that is
    the useful order: `unsetEnvironmentVariable`/`setEnvironmentVariable` check the environment
    name FIRST (ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN @ SCOPE), then the variable name, then the key. Telling
    an operator their environment is unknown is more actionable than telling them a name is
    invalid in an environment that was never going to accept it. Since the browser roster
    restates the closed three, this can only arise on drift - which the e2e arm pins by asserting
    "staging" refuses ENV_ENVIRONMENT_UNKNOWN @ SCOPE.

--- THE THING I DID NOT FIX, DELIBERATELY ---

12. A PAIRED BROWSER CANNOT WRITE. Both environment kinds are in OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS and
    absent from the widening that lets `repository.publish` through, so a paired session READS
    the table (ADMIN) and is refused OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED @ DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION on
    write. Found by the journey, not by reading. I did NOT widen the fence - that is an authority
    decision (same class as the repository.bootstrap widening, which needed an owner ruling).
    Instead: the refusal is given operator words, an arm pins both directions, and the runbook
    states it plainly. The set/unset dialogs work from the daemon host, which is the real
    operator path today.

--- DRILLS, both restored and proved in calls SEPARATE from the restore ---
- environment-variables-screen.tsx (UNTRACKED, so git diff certifies nothing): sha256
  3587c047a0ce67b962315282379b3ad086e29e435dd7b620e2d60da4f0f88248, `grep -c "MUTATION DRILL"` 0.
- live-environment-variables.ts (UNTRACKED): value-detection removed -> the two VALUE_PRESENT arms
  went RED, both of them, including the refusal-envelope one. Restored, sha256
  65edce3f98ce5a0fc8e42bedd2ed8da2f6ffa63d1a005a167ec71f9aa38cc3c3, drill string count 0.
- cordum-app.tsx (TRACKED, so git diff IS valid): stashed for the red-attribution delta, popped,
  `git diff --stat` shows the 5 insertions back, sha256 2de067b7...da74 matches the backup.
Post-restore: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` -> 188 files / 2386 tests EXIT 0.
